title: HCP Engagement Patterns — Access Restrictions and Digital Shift
summary: HCP access restrictions continue to tighten across markets. Digital and remote engagement channels are growing as alternatives to in-person visits.

findings.access_trends: In-person HCP access declining year-over-year across most markets. No-see and restricted-access policies expanding beyond specialists to primary care.
findings.digital_adoption: Digital channel adoption accelerated post-pandemic. Video, approved email, and self-service content portals growing.
findings.rep_expectations: Field reps expected to be multi-channel — in-person, video, email, content sharing within a single customer engagement strategy.
findings.measurement: Engagement quality metrics (content interaction time, response rates, multi-touch attribution) gaining importance alongside visit frequency.

title: Digital Channel Effectiveness Benchmarks
summary: Digital channels show varying effectiveness by therapeutic area and HCP specialty. Approved email has the broadest adoption, video engagement is growing from a smaller base.

approved_email.open_rates: Range from 15-40% depending on specialty and content relevance. Higher for disease education than promotional content.
approved_email.click_rates: 5-15% for well-targeted campaigns. Drops significantly for mass-send approaches.

video_engagement.adoption: Growing but still a fraction of total engagement volume. Higher adoption in specialty care than primary care.
video_engagement.effectiveness: Video meetings show higher content recall and engagement depth than in-person visits in some studies.

content_portals.usage: Self-service HCP content portals see variable adoption. Most effective when integrated with other channels.

title: Omnichannel Maturity and Field Force Evolution
summary: Organizations progressing toward omnichannel engagement face challenges in organizational alignment, data integration, and measurement. Most are at early stages of maturity.

maturity_assessment.current_state: Most organizations at stages 2-4 of omnichannel maturity. Few have achieved fully orchestrated engagement.
maturity_assessment.barriers: Organizational silos (sales vs marketing), data fragmentation, measurement complexity, and content operations capacity.
maturity_assessment.success_factors: Cross-functional governance, unified customer data, flexible content operations, and progressive maturity roadmap.

field_force_evolution.role_changes: Field rep role evolving from call executor to relationship orchestrator managing multiple channels.
field_force_evolution.capability_gaps: Many organizations lack the analytics, content operations, and change management capabilities for advanced omnichannel.
field_force_evolution.training_needs: Reps need training in digital engagement tools, content personalization, and data-driven customer planning.

title: Veeva Pulse 2Q 2022 Field Trends — Channel Mix and Regional Variation
summary: Veeva Pulse 2Q 2022 report based on 600M+ annual HCP-rep interactions. In-person visits dominate globally but significant regional variation exists. The UK is a pronounced outlier with email surpassing face-to-face. Three tiers of rep engagement effectiveness (leading, average, lagging) show widening performance gaps.

findings.global_channel_mix: 73% in-person, 18% email, 9% other (video, phone, chat). In-person recovered from pandemic lows but remains below 2019 levels.
findings.us_channel_mix: 70% in-person, slightly below global average. Digital mix higher in specialty care than primary care.
findings.uk_outlier: 32% in-person vs 43% email — the only major market where email exceeds face-to-face. Driven by NHS access restrictions and established digital workflows.
findings.hcp_digital_preference: 75% of HCPs indicate they want more digital engagement options. Preference strongest in oncology and hospital-based specialties.
findings.rep_performance_tiers: Leading reps (top quartile) achieve 2-3x more meetings per cycle through superior digital channel integration. Lagging reps rely almost entirely on in-person and show declining access rates.
findings.regional_variation: APAC and Latin America show highest in-person percentages (80%+). EU varies significantly by country due to regulatory and healthcare system differences.

source: Veeva Pulse Field Trends Report v10-2 (2Q 2022, July 2022)

title: Veeva Pulse 3Q 2022 Field Trends — Video Effectiveness and Rep Productivity
summary: Veeva Pulse 3Q 2022 report shows HCP accessibility at 60% and video engagement delivering 3x call response rates vs non-video interactions. Digitally-enabled reps achieve 30-40% more meetings. Half of HCPs limit engagement to three or fewer companies, making share of access a critical competitive metric.

findings.hcp_access_rate: 60% of HCPs remain accessible to field reps. Access rate stable quarter-over-quarter but varies sharply by specialty and institution type.
findings.video_effectiveness: Video adds 3x call response rate vs standard in-person or phone outreach. Reps using video get significantly more follow-up engagement.
findings.video_adoption: 50%+ of reps now use video engagement, up from under 20% pre-pandemic. Adoption uneven across companies and therapeutic areas.
findings.company_access_limits: 50% of HCPs limit interactions to 3 or fewer companies. Share of access is now as important as share of voice.
findings.digitally_enabled_reps: Reps who integrate digital channels into their engagement strategy achieve 30-40% more meetings than those relying on in-person alone.
findings.global_channel_mix_3q: 76% in-person, 15% email, 9% other. Slight in-person increase from 2Q as markets continued reopening.
findings.crm_engage_usage: CRM Engage video sessions growing quarter-over-quarter. Most effective when combined with content sharing during the session.

title: Veeva Pulse — Oncology Engagement Patterns and Specialty Divergence
summary: Oncology engagement patterns diverge significantly from primary care. Leading oncology reps use 2.5x more video, send 2x more content, and have 67% longer meetings. Specialty-specific engagement strategies are critical — one-size-fits-all approaches underperform.

findings.oncology_video_usage: Leading oncology reps use 2.5x more video engagement than average reps. Oncology HCPs have higher receptivity to video due to complex data discussions.
findings.content_intensity: Leading oncology reps send 2x more content (clinical reprints, dosing guides, patient resources) than average. Content sharing correlates with meeting acceptance rates.
findings.meeting_duration: Oncology meetings are 67% longer on average than primary care interactions. Reflects complexity of oncology treatment decisions and data discussions.
findings.specialty_divergence: Engagement patterns in oncology, immunology, and rare disease diverge sharply from primary care. Primary care trends toward shorter, higher-frequency touchpoints while specialty moves toward fewer but deeper engagements.
findings.implication_for_crm: CRM platforms must support specialty-specific engagement profiles — content libraries, call planning algorithms, and performance metrics should vary by therapeutic area.

source: Veeva Pulse Field Trends Reports (2Q and 3Q 2022 combined analysis)
